plan.topic: Holiday party drinks on tirzepatide: why a fuller, slower stomach and GI side effects make pacing and fluids matter
plan.angle: Reframe the topic as: 'Holiday drinks on tirzepatide: what the label covers, and simple pacing habits to ask your prescriber about.' Sentence 1 as written. By 6 s: 'The label doesn't specifically address alcohol' (only if confirmed). Then separate label sentences: it delays gastric emptying. Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea are common. Fluid loss from them has been linked to kidney problems (label wording). No 'so' or 'that's why' between them. Caveat clause: low blood sugar risk is higher for people with diabetes on insulin or a sulfonylurea. Untagged tips: sip water alongside, unless you've been told to limit fluids. Eat something with protein. Skipping the drink is fine too. We can't give a safe amount, so ask your prescriber. Emergency card: 'If you have severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, stop using it and call your healthcare provider right away.' Then: 'For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.' Then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. No craving research, no dates.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide at a Holiday Party: What About Drinks? #shorts
plan.why: The playbook's 20:00 holiday-table slot runs 11-18 to 11-27 and lists drinks at a party. Party-season searches are rising, and this angle (stomach and fluids) differs from the 11-12 low-blood-sugar Short. | fact-check: The topic line says 'why a fuller, slower stomach and GI side effects make pacing and fluids matter'. That links gastric emptying to an outcome as cause and effect, which the craft rules ban and the label doesn't support. Drop the 'why'. Alcohol content also carries risks: it reads as a 'safe amount' if hedged badly, and the pancreatitis and low blood sugar framing must stay at label scope. The angle mostly handles this. Keep these conditions. (1) Say the label doesn't specifically address alcohol only after checking the current Zepbound and Mounjaro PIs (28 and 27 Aug 2026) and confirming it. (2) Each label fact gets its own sentence, with no causal link between them. (3) Low blood sugar only for people with diabetes on insulin or a sulfonylurea, stated in the spoken line. (4) Never suggest drinking is expected. Add a no-pressure line such as 'Skipping the drink is always fine too.' (5) Holiday framing is fine for a timed Short, but keep 'this year' and dates out of the narration and on-screen text. The emergency line and the scoped don't-stop line must be copied exactly.

package.title: Holiday Drinks on Tirzepatide: What the Label Flags #shorts
package.description:
The tirzepatide label doesn't cover alcohol. But it flags a few things worth knowing before a holiday party.
Tirzepatide weight trials: nausea in up to 3 in 10, mostly during dose increases, easing over time.
Kidney problems have been reported after dehydration from those side effects.
With diabetes on insulin or a sulfonylurea, low blood sugar risk is higher.
We can't give a safe amount. Sip water alongside, unless you've been told to limit fluids.
If you have severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, stop using it and call your healthcare provider right away. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
Verdict: PASS. Every factual claim matches the current tirzepatide labels on DailyMed (Zepbound revised 28 Aug 2026, Mounjaro revised 27 Aug 2026). I found nothing unsafe and no invented sources. There are three small wording fixes listed below.

What I checked:
- **Nausea stat:** The Zepbound label's Table 1 (Studies 1 and 2 pooled) gives nausea at 25%, 29% and 28% by dose against 8% on placebo. So "up to 3 in 10" and "Up to 29%" are correct.
- **Stomach and GI wording:** Section 12.2 says "Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying." Section 6.1 says the nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea "occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time." The script keeps the stomach-emptying sentence and the side-effects sentence separate, with no "so" linking them.
- **Kidneys:** Acute kidney injury due to volume depletion is section 5.3 in the Zepbound label and 5.5 in the Mounjaro label.
- **Low blood sugar:** The hypoglycaemia line names the right group: people with diabetes taking insulin or a sulfonylurea (Mounjaro 5.3; Zepbound 5.7).
- **Alcohol:** Neither label mentions alcohol or ethanol. The only alcohol in either is benzyl alcohol listed as an ingredient in the Mounjaro vial and KwikPen. So "The label doesn't cover alcohol" is accurate.
- **Safety lines:** The water tip keeps "unless you've been told to limit fluids". The emergency line and the don't-stop line are copied exactly. The script gives no safe amount of alcohol, our own tips carry no source tag, and there's no subscribe line or "link in the description" line.
- **Length:** I count exactly 160 spoken words, with "3" and "10" spoken as words. That is at the 160-word cap, not the "about 159" in the post note. It's still allowed.

issues.claim: Nausea by dose, Zepbound weight trials, vs 8% placebo
issues.problem: A viewer watching without sound can't tell who was in the trials or how long they lasted. Studies 1 and 2 ran for 72 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight, and Study 2 enrolled only people with type 2 diabetes. Our rules say every stat card must name the population and the timeframe.
issues.fix: stat_label: "Nausea by dose, tirzepatide vs 8% placebo, 72-week Zepbound weight trials in adults"

issues.problem: The on-screen card leaves out that the risk is higher, so it says less than the narration does.
